results.reason: Issue 1 covers this in full. It cites Supply Agt §14.2: a change of more than 50% of voting stock is deemed an assignment requiring Vantrell's prior written consent, with a 30-day termination right. It notes the sale transfers 100%, Schedule 4.4 says "None," §4.4(c) is inaccurate, and §6.3/§7.2(c) do not reach the consent.

Issue 15 notes the asymmetry: Corbel cannot assign without consent, while Vantrell may assign to any Person without Corbel's consent. It never explains the risk that the sole-source contract could pass to a competitor or other undesirable party. It only says Vantrell 'can transfer the contract to a third party.'

Issue 2 calculates the 120-day deadline as September 2, 2026 and states it passed before the September 21 SPA date. It says the option cannot be exercised after the deadline and that the contract may expire if no notice was given, so the extension right is at risk.

Issue 3 states Side Letter §2 limits Fundamental Representations to 4.1 and 4.2 and that the Side Letter controls under §11.11. It explains that Capitalization and Taxes lose uncapped treatment under §9.5(b) and become subject to the Deductible and Cap.

Issue 4 identifies the conflict: Side Letter §§6.1–6.2 select Delaware law and Chancery, while SPA §§11.8–11.9 select New York. It explains that indemnity claims would be governed by Delaware under the Side Letter while related disputes could be in New York. Issue 3 separately establishes that the Side Letter takes precedence.
The response states Cap = 10% of the Purchase Price = $8,450,000.
Issue 3 states SPA §11.11 sets the order of precedence as Side Letter first, SPA second.
The memo is addressed to the Supervising Partner. Each issue gives 'Where,' 'Why it matters,' and 'Fix' as separate items.
Issues are ordered Critical, High, Medium, then Clean-up. Part 4 lists the calls needed with the client before responding.
The response says the deadline passed and the option cannot be exercised after it. It never states the window remains open.
The response states the Side Letter controls and that Capitalization and Taxes become capped. It does not make the prohibited statement.
